strengths: Addresses an important and under-explored domain: While Semantic Scene Completion (SSC) is well-established in terrestrial autonomous driving and indoor perception, aerial SSC has been largely unaddressed due to the payload and energy constraints of LiDAR on UAVs.

Well-designed and scalable LiDAR-free ground-truth generation framework: Leveraging photogrammetric SfM/MVS combined with 2D-to-3D label lifting allows accurate 3D semantic voxel grids to be built with manual annotations on fewer than 10% of frames.

Comprehensive dataset diversity and scale: OccuFly contains over 20,000 samples spanning 9 real-world scenes across four seasons, three flight altitudes (30 m, 40 m, 50 m), both nadir and oblique perspectives, and includes dense metric depth maps.

Valuable metric depth benchmark: Fine-tuning Depth-Anything-V2 demonstrates substantial improvements over zero-shot metric estimation in aerial views and establishes a strong depth prior for aerial perception tasks.
weaknesses: Insufficient breadth of benchmarked SSC methods: The paper evaluates only a single baseline architecture (CGFormer). A benchmark paper should ideally compare multiple representative paradigm families (e.g., MonoScene, VoxFormer, Symphonies, or TPVFormer) to assess how different aerial representations (voxel, BEV, TPV) perform under viewpoint changes.

Severe class imbalance and near-zero baseline mIoU: As shown in Tables 6 and 11, 'Building' dominates with ~75.7% of voxels, while many classes (e.g., Person, Cable, Flying Animal, Truck) have less than 0.1% presence. Consequently, CGFormer achieves an overall mIoU of only 0.8% (0.0080), with nearly half of the semantic classes scoring 0.0000. More guidance, class re-weighting baselines, or taxonomy grouping are needed to make this a practical benchmark for the community.

Inherent limitations of photogrammetric pseudo-ground-truth: The SfM/MVS reconstruction fundamentally assumes a static scene, meaning dynamic objects are suppressed or distorted. Furthermore, occluded volumes (e.g., under trees or building eaves) rely heavily on heuristic silhouette carving and Poisson meshing rather than direct physical measurement, which could introduce systematic geometric biases.

Lack of direct 3D geometric validation: Reprojection RMSE (1.24 px) only measures the quality of feature matching in observable 2D images, but does not quantify the volumetric accuracy or completeness of the completed/densified voxels against ground-truth geometry (such as terrestrial LiDAR or high-density survey data).

strengths: Pioneering dataset in an underexplored domain: Semantic Scene Completion (SSC) has almost exclusively been studied in terrestrial autonomous driving and indoor scenes. OccuFly addresses an important gap by introducing the first real-world, aerial camera-based SSC dataset.

Well-designed and scalable LiDAR-free data generation pipeline: By combining SfM/MVS with 2D-to-3D semantic lifting (annotating <10% of images and projecting via multi-view correspondences), followed by class-aware densification (Poisson reconstruction for ground, DBSCAN + visual hull carving for instances), the framework effectively circumvents the heavy payload and sparsity issues of aerial LiDAR.

Comprehensive data modalities and multi-altitude coverage: The dataset contains over 20,000 samples across 9 diverse scenes, 4 seasons, and 3 altitudes (30m, 40m, 50m), complete with calibrated camera poses, dense metric depth maps, and 22 semantic classes.

Valuable metric depth contribution: Generating dense metric depth maps and fine-tuning Depth-Anything-V2 on the aerial domain provides an immediately useful asset for aerial vision researchers, demonstrating strong performance improvements over out-of-the-box monocular metric estimators.

Clarity and transparency: The methodology, filtering steps, frustum-culling, and reprojection errors are clearly documented, and the paper includes extensive supplementary visualizations and scene statistics.
weaknesses: Limited benchmark breadth for the primary task (SSC): The paper evaluates only a single SSC model (CGFormer). For a benchmark contribution, it is standard practice to evaluate multiple representative paradigms (e.g., MonoScene, VoxFormer, TPVFormer, Symphonies) to understand how different architectural designs (planar vs. voxel, depth-conditioned vs. direct feature projection) handle elevated viewpoints.

Severe class imbalance and low baseline semantic performance: CGFormer achieves an overall mIoU of only 0.8% (0.0080) and 0.0000 across many minority classes (e.g., person, bicycle, cables, cranes, truck). While the dominance of 'Building' (75.7%) reflects real aerial statistics, the paper would be significantly strengthened by exploring basic mitigation strategies (e.g., class-balanced focal loss, voxel re-weighting, or group-level metrics) to provide a more competitive baseline.

Dataset diversity constrained by scene count: Although the dataset boasts over 20,000 frames, these are captured from 9 localized scenes in a single geographic region. Because frames within a flight pattern have high spatial overlap, the effective structural diversity is somewhat limited.

Coarse voxel resolution for fine-grained classes: A voxel resolution of r = 0.5m is relatively large for classes such as person, bicycle, and cables, where an entire object spans only 1–2 voxels. This likely contributes to the near-zero IoU on these categories and deserves deeper discussion.

strengths: Introduction of a timely and novel task domain: semantic scene completion (SSC) has almost exclusively focused on ground-level autonomous driving datasets (SemanticKITTI, Occ3D, OpenOccupancy), making an aerial UAV-centric SSC benchmark a valuable direction for low-altitude robotics and surveillance.

Well-motivated LiDAR-free data generation pipeline: using multi-view photogrammetry/SfM-MVS with 2D-to-3D label lifting via correspondence and class-aware densification (silhouette carving for instances and Poisson surface reconstruction for terrain) effectively sidesteps the payload/power constraints of UAV LiDARs.

Scale and environmental diversity: the dataset provides over 20,000 multi-altitude (30m, 40m, 50m) frames across 9 scenes covering four seasons and three environment types (urban, industrial, rural) with a rich 22-class taxonomy.

Comprehensive auxiliary assets: providing metric depth maps alongside 3D semantic voxel grids and fine-tuning Depth-Anything-V2 provides a valuable dual benchmark for both aerial depth estimation and volumetric completion.
weaknesses: Insufficient SSC baseline benchmarking: as a benchmark paper, evaluating only a single SSC method (CGFormer) is a significant limitation. A rigorous benchmark should compare multiple representative paradigms (e.g., planar BEV/TPV methods like TPVFormer, voxel-query transformers like VoxFormer, and baseline optics-based approaches like MonoScene).

Extremely low SSC performance without deep diagnostic analysis: the baseline achieves an overall mIoU of only 0.80% (Table 11), with 14 out of 22 classes scoring 0.0000 or below 0.0010. While aerial SSC is challenging, having near-zero performance across the majority of classes limits the benchmark's immediate diagnostic utility, and the manuscript lacks architectural adaptations or targeted loss formulations to address this.

Severe class imbalance: the dataset exhibits extreme frequency disparity (e.g., 'Building' occupies ~75.7% of voxels, while 8 classes account for less than 0.01% each), which directly contributes to model collapse on underrepresented categories. The paper does not provide reweighting strategies or grouped evaluation metrics to make the benchmark more informative.

Artifacts and assumptions inherent to photogrammetric ground truth: relying on offline SfM/MVS enforces a strict static-world assumption that eliminates dynamic objects (e.g., moving vehicles or pedestrians), while silhouette carving and Poisson reconstruction can introduce geometric bloat or oversmoothing on fine structures (such as cables, thin poles, and vegetation).

strengths: Pioneering contribution: OccuFly establishes the first real-world 3D Semantic Scene Completion (SSC) benchmark tailored to the low-altitude aerial domain, addressing a noticeable gap in a literature largely dominated by terrestrial autonomous driving and indoor scenes.

Efficient and practical LiDAR-free data generation pipeline: The proposed methodology circumvents the payload and energy constraints of UAV-mounted LiDAR by utilizing photogrammetric SfM/MVS reconstruction. The semi-automated label propagation framework—annotating less than 10% of keyframes to cover over 99% of 3D points—is well-motivated and saves substantial 3D manual annotation effort.

Rigorous data validation: The authors validate the reconstruction and labeling quality via multiple checks, including reprojection errors (1.24 px RMS), label transfer accuracy on 135 held-out annotated frames (92% pixel-wise agreement), and detailed comparisons against modern 2D/3D foundation models.

Valuable dual benchmarking: In addition to SSC, the dataset provides dense metric depth maps across multiple altitudes (30m, 40m, 50m) and seasons. The benchmarking of monocular metric depth foundation models (Depth-Anything-v2/v3, Metric3D-v2) convincingly highlights severe zero-shot domain gaps and proves that fine-tuning on OccuFly yields dramatic improvements.
Clarity and completeness: The submission and supplementary materials provide comprehensive statistical breakdowns, class taxonomies, DBSCAN hyperparameter tables, and scene-level visual outputs.
weaknesses: Geographic diversity is somewhat limited: While the dataset contains over 20,000 image/voxel/depth samples, they are derived from 9 reconstructed scenes within a single metropolitan area (Ingolstadt, Germany). Splitting across scenes (5 train, 2 val, 2 test) is the right protocol to prevent leakage, but evaluating test performance on only two scenes risks sensitivity to local site-specific characteristics.

Severe baseline performance degradation: The evaluated SSC baselines (DISC and Symphonies) achieve very low semantic accuracy (mIoU of 2.04% and 0.58%, respectively), with most tail classes scoring near 0%. While this demonstrates the substantial domain gap between ground-vehicle and aerial SSC, it leaves open whether terrestrial model architectures are fundamentally ill-suited or whether issues like extreme class imbalance (buildings alone account for ~75% of voxels) and voxel resolution (0.5m) need aerial-specific re-formulation or architectural adjustments.

Static scene assumption and reconstruction artifacts: Because the ground truth depends on multi-view photogrammetric reconstruction, dynamic objects (e.g., moving vehicles or pedestrians) cannot be reliably reconstructed and are suppressed or excluded, limiting the representation of dynamic traffic elements essential for practical UAV navigation.

strengths: Pioneering Aerial SSC Benchmark: The paper introduces OccuFly, the first real-world camera-based 3D semantic scene completion (SSC) benchmark designed specifically for low-altitude aerial robotics, successfully addressing an important gap in the predominantly terrestrial-focused SSC literature.

Cost-Effective and Scalable Annotation Framework: The proposed data generation pipeline circumvents the mass and power constraints of aerial LiDAR by leveraging multi-view photogrammetry (SfM+MVS) and 2D-to-3D label lifting. By annotating less than 10% of 2D images, the pipeline achieves >99% 3D point coverage, supported by class-aware object densification (visual hull carving and Poisson reconstruction).

Thorough Pipeline Verification: The reconstruction quality is validated with low average reprojection errors (1.24 px) and a 92% semantic agreement on held-out manually annotated test frames across varying altitudes and scenes.

Dual Task Benchmarking: Beyond SSC, the dataset provides over 20,000 dense metric depth maps and benchmarks modern monocular foundation models (Metric3Dv2, Depth-Anything v2/v3, MapAnything). The depth fine-tuning experiments demonstrate clear practical utility and show substantial metric error reductions.

Comprehensive Documentation: The paper and supplementary material provide detailed implementation specifics, per-scene reprojection errors, class frequency analyses, and altitude-wise ablation studies.
weaknesses: Limited Geographic Diversity: While the dataset contains over 20,000 frames, these are captured across only 9 distinct physical scenes in a single geographic region (Ingolstadt, Germany). Because aerial double-grid flight patterns yield high overlap (>90%), frame-to-frame redundancy within each scene is high, and evaluating generalization on only 2 test scenes is somewhat limited.

Severe Baseline Performance Floor in SSC: The evaluated terrestrial SSC models (Symphonies and DISC) achieve extremely poor semantic performance (mIoU between 0.58% and 2.20%), with many classes scoring near 0.00%. While this effectively demonstrates a large domain gap, the paper does not offer an aerial-tailored baseline or in-depth ablation into the causes (e.g., whether this failure stems primarily from extreme class imbalance, voxel discretization resolution, or single-view feature projection limitations).

Coarse Voxel Resolution for Fine-Grained Classes: The chosen voxel size of r = 0.5 m is relatively large compared to standard terrestrial benchmarks (typically 0.2 m). For small object classes such as 'person', 'bicycle', and 'cable'—which also suffer from extreme rarity (<0.01% occurrence)—a 0.5 m grid significantly limits geometric precision and recognition feasibility.

Assumption of Static Scenes: The reconstruction and silhouette-carving pipeline relies heavily on static multi-view consistency. While acknowledged by the authors, dynamic agents (e.g., moving traffic, pedestrians) are either filtered out or risk introducing ghosting artifacts into the volumetric ground truth.

strengths: Addresses an important and underexplored problem: bringing 3D Semantic Scene Completion (SSC) from terrestrial autonomous driving to the low-altitude aerial (UAV) domain.

Proposes a well-designed, LiDAR-free data generation pipeline combining SfM/MVS multi-view reconstruction with class-aware densification (silhouette carving for instances and Poisson surface reconstruction for terrain) and an efficient 2D-to-3D label-lifting strategy requiring manual annotation of <10% of frames.
Provides multi-faceted ground truth, including dense metric depth maps and 21 semantic classes across varying flight altitudes (30m, 40m, 50m) and multiple seasons.
Evaluates both SSC models and recent metric depth foundation models (e.g., Depth-Anything-v2/v3, Metric3D, MapAnything), clearly exposing the significant terrestrial-to-aerial domain gap.
weaknesses: Limited geographic scene diversity: although the dataset contains over 20,000 camera frames, they are captured across only 9 distinct geographic scenes in one metropolitan region (Ingolstadt, Germany). Splitting across only 9 scenes (5 train, 2 val, 2 test) risks significant overfitting and limited environment generalization.

Extremely low SSC baseline performance: DISC achieves only 2.04% mIoU and Symphonies achieves 0.58% mIoU, with 15 out of 21 semantic classes registering 0.00% IoU. While this demonstrates task difficulty, the lack of tailored loss weighting or architectural adaptation leaves open whether modern SSC frameworks can feasibly learn this benchmark without collapsing to dominant classes.

Severe class imbalance: 'Building' accounts for over 62% (and ~75% in the test set) of occupied voxels, while several classes (e.g., person, bicycle, cable, cable tower) represent <0.01%, contributing heavily to the near-zero IoU on non-building classes.

Assumption of purely static scenes: because ground-truth generation relies on classical multi-view stereo, moving objects (vehicles in motion, walking pedestrians) cannot be reconstructed accurately, limiting applicability to dynamic real-world flight operations.

Reliance on commercial software: the core 3D reconstruction step utilizes proprietary closed-source software (Agisoft Metashape 2.2.0) rather than open-source tools (e.g., COLMAP), creating potential hurdles for community replication and extension of the data generation pipeline.
